arxiv-2111-03691.title: The Ball Pit Algorithm: A Markov Chain Monte Carlo Method Based on Path Integrals
arxiv-2111-03691.creator: Miguel Fudolig
arxiv-2111-03691.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Miguel Fudolig. The Ball Pit Algorithm (BPA) is a novel Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm for sampling marginal posterior distributions developed from the path integral formulation of the Bayesian analysis for Markov chains. The BPA yielded comparable results to the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo as implemented by the adaptive No U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) in sampling posterior distributions for simulated data from Bernoulli and Poisson likelihoods.

arxiv-2210-00436.title: Inductive Freeness of Ziegler’s Canonical Multiderivations for Restrictions of Reflection Arrangements
arxiv-2210-00436.creator: Torsten Hoge, Gerhard Röhrle, and Sven Wiesner
arxiv-2210-00436.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Torsten Hoge, Gerhard Röhrle, and Sven Wiesner. Let 𝒜 {\mathscr{A}} be a free hyperplane arrangement. In 1989, Ziegler showed that the restriction 𝒜 ′′ {\mathscr{A}}^{\prime\prime} of 𝒜 {\mathscr{A}} to any hyperplane endowed with the natural multiplicity κ \kappa is then a free multiarrangement. Recently, in [ HR25 ] , an analogue of Ziegler’s theorem for the stronger notion of inductive freeness was proved: if 𝒜 {\mathscr{A}} is inductively free, then so is the free multiarrangement ( 𝒜 ′′ , κ ) ({\mathscr{A}}^{\prime\prime},\kappa) .

arxiv-2308-03611.title: On global attraction to solitons for 3D Maxwell-Lorentz equations
arxiv-2308-03611.description: Abstract We consider the Maxwell field coupled to a single rotating charge. This Hamiltonian system admits soliton-type solutions, where the field is static, while the charge rotates with constant angular velocity. We prove that any solution of finite energy converges, in suitable local energy seminorms, to the corresponding soliton in the long time limit t → ± ∞ t\to\pm\infty .

arxiv-2405-19117.title: ChartFormer: A Large Vision Language Model for Converting Chart Images into Tactile Accessible SVGs
arxiv-2405-19117.creator: Omar Moured, Sara Alzalabny, Anas Osman, Thorsten Schwarz, Karin Müller, Rainer Stiefelhagen
arxiv-2405-19117.description: Abstract Visualizations, such as charts, are crucial for interpreting complex data. However, they are often provided as raster images, which are not compatible with assistive technologies for people with blindness and visual impairments, such as embossed papers or tactile displays. At the same time, creating accessible vector graphics requires a skilled sighted person and is time-intensive.

arxiv-2501-10854.title: Achievable DoF Bounds for Cache-Aided Asymmetric MIMO Communications Thanks: This work was supported by Infotech Oulu and by the Research Council of Finland under grants no. 343586 (CAMAIDE) and 346208 (6G Flagship).
arxiv-2501-10854.creator: Mohammad NaseriTehrani, MohammadJavad Salehi, and Antti Tölli
arxiv-2501-10854.description: Abstract Integrating coded caching (CC) into multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications can significantly enhance the achievable degrees of freedom (DoF) in wireless networks. This paper investigates a practical cache-aided asymmetric MIMO configuration with cache ratio γ \gamma , where a server equipped with L L transmit antennas communicates with K K users, each having G k G_{k} receive antennas.

arxiv-2502-17423.title: S4S: Solving for a Diffusion Model Solver
arxiv-2502-17423.creator: Eric Frankel, Sitan Chen, Jerry Li ∗, Pang Wei Koh ∗, Lillian J. Ratliff ∗, Sewoong Oh ∗
arxiv-2502-17423.description: Abstract Diffusion models (DMs) create samples from a data distribution by starting from random noise and iteratively solving a reverse-time ordinary differential equation (ODE). Because each step in the iterative solution requires an expensive neural function evaluation (NFE), there has been significant interest in approximately solving these diffusion ODEs with only a few NFEs without modifying the underlying model.

arxiv-2505-22019.title: VRAG-RL: Empower Vision-Perception-Based RAG for Visually Rich Information Understanding via Iterative Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2505-22019.creator: Qiuchen Wang, Ruixue Ding, Yu Zeng, Zehui Chen, Lin Chen, Shihang Wang, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang, Feng Zhao Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group
arxiv-2505-22019.description: Abstract Effectively retrieving, reasoning and understanding visually rich information remains a challenge for traditional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) methods. On the one hand, traditional text-based methods cannot handle visual-related information. On the other hand, current vision-based RAG approaches are often limited by fixed pipelines and frequently struggle to reason effectively due to the insufficient activation of the fundamental capabilities of models.

arxiv-2506-07237.title: Multi-Distillation from Speech and Music Representation Models
arxiv-2506-07237.creator: Jui-Chiang Wei ∗, Yi-Cheng Lin ∗, Fabian Ritter-Gutierrez, Hung-yi Lee
arxiv-2506-07237.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jui-Chiang Wei ∗, Yi-Cheng Lin ∗, Fabian Ritter-Gutierrez, Hung-yi Lee. Real-world audio often mixes speech and music, yet models typically handle only one domain. This paper introduces a multi-teacher distillation framework that unifies speech and music models into a single one while significantly reducing model size. Our approach leverages the strengths of domain-specific teacher models, such as HuBERT for speech and MERT for music, and explores various strategies to balance both domains.

arxiv-2509-10762.title: AI Answer Engine Citation Behavior: Bringing the GEO-16 Framework in B2B SaaS
arxiv-2509-10762.creator: Arlen Kumar University of California, Berkeley Wrodium Research Leanid Palkhouski University of California, Berkeley Wrodium Research
arxiv-2509-10762.description: Abstract 1 Abstract AI answer engines are becoming primary distribution channels for B2B SaaS knowledge, yet determinants of which pages they cite remain under - studied. We introduce GEO - 16 , a 16 - pillar auditing framework that quantifies page quality signals relevant to citation behavior.

arxiv-2601-06630.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Molla Basir Ahamed, Sujoy Majumder ∗ and Nabadwip Sarkar. This paper is devoted to the investigation of multidimensional analogues of refined Bohr-type inequalities for bounded holomorphic mappings on the unit polydisc 𝔻 n \mathbb{D}^{n} . We establish a sharp extension of the classical Bohr inequality, proving that the Bohr radius remains R n = 1 / ( 3 ​ n ) R_{n}=1/(3n) for the family of holomorphic functions bounded by unity in the multivariate setting.

arxiv-2602-20800.title: Mitigating Preference Leakage via Strict Estimator Separation for Normative Generative Ranking CCS: Information systems Information retrieval CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning approaches
arxiv-2602-20800.creator: Dalia Nahhas, Xiaohao Cai, Imran Razzak, Shoaib Jameel
arxiv-2602-20800.description: Abstract . In Generative Information Retrieval (GenIR), the bottleneck has shifted from generation to the selection of candidates, particularly for normative criteria such as cultural relevance. Current LLM-as-a-Judge evaluations often suffer from circularity and preference leakage, where overlapping supervision and evaluation models inflate performance.

pmc-10626022.creator: Patcharapun Sarisuta, Issarapa Chunsuwan, Tippawan Hansakunachai, Paskorn Sritipsukho
pmc-10626022.description: Background Reading disorder is the most common comorbid condition with attention-deficit/hyperactive-impulsive disorder (ADHD) in school-aged children.Purpose This study compared symptoms of ADHD among children in grade 1 at risk of reading disorder with children not at risk.Methods This cross-sectional study included 703 students in grade 1 aged 6–8 years from 8 schools in Pathumthani Province, Thailand, in 2019.

pmc-10750738.title: Prevalence of Salmonella species and factors associated with contamination of mechanically recovered poultry meat imported into South Africa, 2016–2017
pmc-10750738.creator: Tandile Nwabisa Ndobeni, Kudakwashe Magwedere, Daniel Nenene Qekwana
pmc-10750738.description: Background and Aim:Mechanically recovered meat (MRM) products have been linked to outbreaks of human salmonellosis. Therefore, this study aimed to estimate the prevalence and factors associated with Salmonella spp.

pmc-11608597.title: Personalized Medicine in Histiocytic Disorders: Novel Targets in Patients Without MAPK Alterations
pmc-11608597.creator: Katherine ER Smith, Aldo A Acosta-Medina, Surendra Dasari, Wasantha Ranatunga, Karen L Rech, Aishwarya Ravindran, Jason R Young, Patrick W McGarrah, Gordon J Ruan, Saurabh S Zanwar, Jenny J Li, Julio C Sartori-Valinotti, Jessica N Snider, Thomas E Witzig, Gaurav Goyal, Ronald S Go, Jithma P Abeykoon
pmc-11608597.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PURPOSEBRAF and MEK inhibitors are standard treatments in histiocytic disorders, such as Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD). Some patients lack MAPK-pathway alterations, making these treatments less effective.METHODSWe describe three patients with histiocytic disorders who have novel non-MAPK pathway alterations. These alterations were studied through genomic and in silico analyses when applicable, then treated with off-label medications rationally selected on the basis of genomic alterations.RESULTSPatient 1 had rapidly progressive ECD involving the CNS.

pmc-11680320.title: Analysis of Implementation Strategies for Nationwide HPV Vaccination Programs Across European Union Countries
pmc-11680320.creator: Wojciech Miazga, Tomasz Tatara, Mariusz Gujski, Janusz Ostrowski, Jarosław Pinkas, Urszula Religioni
pmc-11680320.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background/Objectives: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programs play a critical role in the primary prevention of HPV-related diseases, including cervical cancer. However, the principles governing the implementation of these programs vary across European Union (EU) countries. The objective of this study was to analyze and compare the strategies for implementing HPV vaccination programs across the EU, with a focus on access, vaccine selection, and procurement processes.

pmc-12414180.title: LDL-C achievement in patients with coronary artery disease: a study protocol for the EDHIPO-MARCA retrospective registry
pmc-12414180.creator: Brayan Daniel Cordoba-Melo, Juan Pablo Arango-Ibanez, Santiago Posso-Marín, Álvaro J Ruiz, Dora Inés Molina, Juan Esteban Gomez-Mesa
pmc-12414180.description: AbstractIntroductionElevated lipid profiles increase the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Despite the availability of lipid-lowering therapy (LLT), adherence to therapy and achievement of Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol (LDL-C) target levels remain suboptimal. Coronary artery disease (CAD) presents substantial public health challenges, with LDL-C goal attainment rates reported to be between 30.0% and 54.0%.

pmc-12509563.title: Complete genome of the Alkalibacterium sp. f15 isolated from Daihai Lake in Inner Mongolia
pmc-12509563.creator: Kai Jiang, Gen Che, Bo Yuan, Chunling Cao, Yanxing Wang, Lijia Ye, Yu Hong
pmc-12509563.description: We isolated a strain of the genus Alkalibacterium from Daihai Lake in Inner Mongolia. The complete genome size is 2,614,554 bp, with a genomic DNA G + C content of 39.3%. Metabolic pathway analysis indicates that strain f15 is a potential lactic acid-fermenting bacterium with industrial applications in lactate fermentation.

pmc-13199664.title: Enhancing immunotherapy efficacy of hepatocellular carcinoma by inhibiting the key antioxidant factor Nrf2
pmc-13199664.creator: Yan Zhu, Maoxuan Liu, Hang Fai Kwok, Liang Chen
pmc-13199664.description: r ImmunoTherapy of Cancer, we show that nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), a master antioxidant transcription factor, acts as a dual suppressor of antitumor immunity in HCC by simultaneously driving programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) expression and silencing major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) on tumor cells.

pmc-13599295.title: A multinational cross-sectional survey on the use of AI-based voice assistance systems in emergency medical services
pmc-13599295.creator: Clemens Möllenhoff, Oddvar Uleberg, Matthias Bender, Thomas Neumuth, Max Rockstroh
pmc-13599295.description: BackgroundEmergency medical services (EMS) worldwide face increasing demands that require improvements in efficiency and quality of care. Voice assistance systems (VAS) based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) can support staff in prehospital settings through contactless, intuitive operation. However, evidence regarding their application in EMS is limited but desired.
